added_lines: mon - wed. 9.00am - 12. 30pm we celebrate today the feast of all saints, not jus t the canonized, but all those people who have been faithful witnesses to the love of god by living out the message of the gospel during their life. we trust that our loved ones, relations and friends are among those who are now enjoying the glory and happiness of being face to face with god. the saints we celeb rate were men and women like us. perhaps we may sometimes think of our departed loved ones as being dead and gone. but our faith helps us to believe that they are alive now more than ever, bec ause they are now fully alive in god. the life they now enjoy can no longer be touched by sickness, su ffering, sin, or death. we thank god for all those whom he has already welcomed to heaven. during november we pray especially for those who are still being purified in purgatory knowing that our prayers can help them. the second reading from the first leʃer of st john, reminds us of the great love of god who already has chosen to call us his children. “what we are to be in the future has not yet been r evealed; all we know is, that when it is revealed, we will be like him, because we will see him as he is." the beatitudes in today’s gospel, propose to us a way of life, inviting us to be poor in spirit, that is relying on god to help us through life, to identify with the meek, those who mourn, and those who hunger and thirst after justice. they challenge us to be compassionate people, to be men and women who are in heart, and to become peacemakers in our deal ings with one another, in our families and in society at large, even when this entails ridicule and persecution. we pray for faith and courage to walk this journey. the saints encourage us in ourd ay-to-day struggles because like us they also endur ed struggles. our faith assures us that all who respond to the lord’s invitation to live the life of the beatitudes will one day hear those welcoming and consoling words, "well done, good and faithful serv ant, enter into the joy of your family of parishes of: ballincollig | ballinora | kilmurry | ovens and farran scan for website discoverya faith evangelist john says in 10;10 'have life and have it all in its fullness'. 1 hour per week for 6 weeks. 2 small groups of 6 participants each. wednesday (men) thursdays (women) initial contact: fr alan o’leary pp or any priest in the family of parishes of ballinora, ballincollig, ovens/farran & kilmurry or derval 083 184 74 79 michael 087 218 52 82 the beatitudes in today’s gospel are the teachings of jesus in the sermon on the mount jesus teaches us that if we live ac- cording to the beatitudes, we will live a happy christian life. the beatitudes fulfil god’s promises made to abraham and his descendants and describe the rewards that will be o urs as loyal followers of christ. blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the k ingdom of heaven. blessed are they who mourn, for they will be comforted. blessed are the meek, for they will inherit the land. blessed are they who hunger and thirst for righteousness, for they will be satisfied. blessed are the merciful, for they will be shown me rcy. blessed are the clean in heart, for they will see god. blessed are the peacemakers, for they will be called children of god. blessed are they who are persecuted for the sake of righteousness, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven . prayer for vocations loving god, at baptism you have gifted each of us with a call to serve you and all people in everything we do. give us the strength to share your message of love, justice, hope and peace in every part of our diocese of cork and ross. we ask you lord, for the gift of new vocations to priesthood in our diocese. in your fatherly care, accompany those who are seeking to know your will for them. inspire those you invite to serve as priests and fill them with the courage to answer that call. throu gh christ our lord, amen. ballincollig
